Laura / team —

Draft technical language and economics below (short version):

SLA (baseline): Redwood guarantees 99th percentile inference latency <= 120ms for requests routed to the Acme reserved pool at 650 tokens/sec baseline for business hours (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 PT). Credits: service credit up to 10% of monthly committed fees for SLA misses measured at the account level.

Overflow behavior (Soft Overflow model):
- When reserved capacity reaches 95% utilization for >30s, new requests will spill to on-demand host pools (same model family/quantization).
- On-demand spillover will be billed at the overflow rate: $0.045 per 1k tokens.
- Monthly customer-controlled spend cap for overflow: default $12,000 (can be configured). When the cap is reached, Redwood will (a) notify primary contact, (b) apply a temporary throttle to non-critical routes for remainder of billing cycle unless customer requests override.
- Hard cap option (customer requested): when reached, all overflow requests are rejected with 503 and a configurable fallback model is used where available.

Observability / billing labels:
- We provide per-route token counts, per-model token counts, and daily CSV exports to Acme's S3 (or direct report in Console).

Operational notes: KV cache warmup and continuous batching can affect short-term latency spikes — the SLA measures steady-state 99th pct. We'll include a 5-minute grace window around scheduled maintenance.

I attached a sample throughput table (throughput-sla-table.csv) and a redline snippet for the amendment. Pricing line for reserved GPU uplift (8x A100-eq) is included; see attachment.

—Dev
